da4281fee8379b88.description:
About the role
0G is hiring its first dedicated DevOps engineer to own our cloud platform end to end: infrastructure, deployments, networking, security hygiene and cost. Today that work is spread across several developers.
Our platform runs on five providers: Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, AWS, Cloudflare and Vercel. It includes:
• 
Validator, seed, RPC, and archive nodes for our mainnet and testnet
• 
Confidential-computing (TEE) workloads, GPU machines and storage nodes
• 
Kubernetes clusters and managed databases
• 
A global RPC load balancer at the edge, and our web apps
All together, that is more than 200 virtual machines. You will be the person who knows what runs where, why it runs there, and what it costs.

What you'll own
You own the platform, from the network edge to the bill.
• 
Cloud operations: provisioning, upgrades, capacity and the full resource lifecycle on Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud and AWS. That includes rightsizing and releasing what nobody uses.
• 
Kubernetes: run, upgrade and scale our clusters. Keep them on supported versions and design node pools, autoscaling and Spot capacity.
• 
Blockchain node fleet: operate validator, sentry, seed, RPC and archive nodes, including peering topology, snapshots, sync and client upgrades.
• 
Networking and edge: VPC design, load balancers, DNS, Cloudflare Workers, Tunnels and WAF, and keeping internet egress deliberate and cheap.
• 
Infrastructure as code and CI/CD: every environment defined in Terraform or Pulumi. You design and run CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent such as GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, covering builds, tests, security scans and releases from commit to production, with no manual steps.
• 
Observability and on-call: metrics, logs, alerts and dashboards, including control of metric cardinality. You also run incident response and write the postmortems.
• 
Security and access: least-privilege IAM across every provider, secrets management, and no databases or admin ports open to the internet.
• 
Cost management: billing exports, budgets and alerts, tagging, a monthly cost review and commitment planning.
• 
Developer enablement: templates, preview environments, documentation and support for the engineers who ship on the platform.
Our stack
Kubernetes: GKE, EKS, Helm, Ingress and Gateway API, autoscaling, RBAC, network policies
Networking: TCP/IP, subnets and CIDR, routing, NAT, L4 and L7 load balancers, DNS, TLS, firewalls, VPC peering
Google Cloud: Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud SQL, Cloud Run, IAM, Cloud Monitoring, billing export to BigQuery
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Pulumi
CI/CD and containers: Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), Argo CD, Docker and BuildKit, container registries
Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Cloud Monitoring, CloudWatch, Alibaba CloudMonitor
Linux: Systems administration, systemd, disks and filesystems, performance debugging
Alibaba Cloud: ECS, VPC, NLB and ALB, ESSD disks, RDS, PolarDB, SAE, Cloud Firewall
AWS: EC2, EKS, RDS, ALB and NLB, Route 53, S3, Organizations
Cloudflare: DNS, Workers, Tunnels, WAF and rate limiting, Zero Trust
Databases (operations): PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, managed Kafka
Blockchain nodes: CometBFT-based chains, reth and other EVM clients, P2P networking
Vercel: Projects, builds, ISR, team access
Confidential computing: Intel TDX virtual machines on Google Cloud and Alibaba Cloud

Must-haves
• 
We want 5+ years in DevOps, SRE or platform roles, including 3+ years running production Kubernetes and owning CI/CD pipelines.
Kubernetes, in depth
• 
Upgrading control planes and node pools with no downtime, and keeping clusters on supported versions.
• 
Scheduling: requests and limits, affinity, taints and tolerations, priority, and eviction under node pressure.
• 
Autoscaling with the HPA, cluster autoscaler or Karpenter, plus Spot or preemptible node pools for non-critical work.
• 
Networking inside the cluster: CNI, Services, Ingress or Gateway API, network policies, and DNS within the cluster.
• 
Security: RBAC, Pod Security, workload identity, and secrets that never sit in plain environment variables.
• 
Stateful workloads: StatefulSets, persistent volumes and CSI drivers, and backup and restore.
• 
Packaging and delivery with Helm or Kustomize, ideally through GitOps with Argo CD or Flux.
• 
Debugging a failing pod, node or rollout from events, logs and metrics.
CI/CD, in depth
• 
Pipeline design: you have built and run production CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Tekton). Pipelines are defined as code in a Jenkinsfile or workflow YAML, with shared libraries and reusable templates.
• 
CI platform operations: running Jenkins controllers with ephemeral agents on Kubernetes, or self-hosted runners. That includes plugin and version upgrades, credential handling, and scaling build capacity.
• 
Build pipelines: multi-service and monorepo builds with caching and parallel stages, and versioned artifacts. Container images built with Docker, BuildKit or Kaniko, including multi-architecture images, image scanning, SBOMs and signing.
• 
Deployment pipelines: promotion from dev to staging to production with approvals and quality gates, plus blue-green, canary and fast rollback. GitOps with Argo CD or Flux, and database migrations as part of a release.
• 
Infrastructure pipelines: Terraform or Pulumi plan and apply from CI, with policy checks and drift detection.
• 
Pipeline security: short-lived credentials through OIDC federation or a secrets vault instead of long-lived keys, least-privilege deploy roles, and protected branches.
• 
Release engineering for our chain: building and publishing node binaries and images, and coordinating rolling upgrades across validator and RPC fleets.
• 
Delivery health: you track build time, build cost, flaky tests and DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, time to restore), and you cut wasted builds with ignore rules and caching.
Networking fundamentals
• 
TCP/IP, subnetting and CIDR, routing, NAT, and the difference between L4 and L7 load balancing.
• 
DNS, TLS and certificates, firewalls and security groups.
• 
Private connectivity: VPC design, peering, private endpoints, and keeping internal traffic off public IPs.
• 
Troubleshooting with dig, curl, mtr and tcpdump, and understanding what internet egress costs.
Also required
• 
Production experience on at least two of Google Cloud, AWS and Alibaba Cloud, and willingness to learn the third quickly.
• 
Terraform or Pulumi in production, plus scripting in Bash and in Python or Go.
• 
A track record of cutting a cloud bill with data, through rightsizing, cleanup or commitments.
• 
A security-first habit with production credentials, and clear written communication.
Nice to have
• 
Running blockchain nodes in production, such as CometBFT validators and sentries, EVM archive or RPC nodes, and snapshot pipelines.
• 
Cloudflare Workers, Tunnels and Zero Trust at scale.
• 
Alibaba Cloud on the international site, including its billing and support model.
• 
Confidential computing (Intel TDX) and GPU workloads.
• 
CKA or CKS certification, a FinOps certification, or experience moving a team between CI systems, such as Jenkins to GitHub Actions.
• 
Go or Rust, enough to read and patch the services you operate.

What we offer
• 
Purpose: The opportunity to contribute to making AI a public good
• 
Growth: A self-directed environment where you can take initiative to shape your role and career
• 
Compensation: Market-competitive compensation including, for most roles, exposure to pre-launch tokens
In addition, 0G Labs is committed to the health and well being of all of our team members. To that end, we provide reimbursements towards a holistic set of experiences and courses:
• 
Core self: Transcendental Meditation
• 
Mind: Landmark Education
• 
Emotion: Art of Communication
• 
Presence: Speech Coach
• 
Body: Fitness, gym and exercise memberships/classes

About Sarvam
Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India, a full-stack sovereign AI platform spanning research, models, infrastructure, and applications, with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. We partner with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role
We are looking for a sharp, high-ownership Marketing Intern to act as the primary story-builder and content engine across Sarvam’s marketing channels.
This is not a passive internship focused on surface-level social updates. You will translate complex frontier AI capabilities like our Vision APIs, Document Intelligence models, and voice platforms into crisp, high-impact stories, viral launch threads, and sharp enterprise collateral. You will sit at the intersection of product, creative execution, and creator operations, helping shape how Sarvam communicates its sovereign AI vision to technical builders, enterprise buyers, and the broader ecosystem.

What You'll Do
Customer Stories & Launch Comms
• 
Transform technical milestones into narratives: Turn enterprise customer deployments into compelling case studies and written success stories.
• 
Drive product launch comms: Draft multi-channel launch content—from sharp X/LinkedIn feature threads to enterprise mailers for prospects and existing clients.
• 
Simplify the complex: Translate technical AI concepts into clear, punchy prose without losing accuracy or depth.
Social Content & Video Operations
• 
Drive video execution: Write scripts for explainer videos and product walkthroughs; coordinate shoots and post-production workflows.
• 
Manage multi-platform publishing: Oversee daily social presence across X, LinkedIn, Instagram, and YouTube, ensuring high content velocity and visual quality.
Creator & Influencer Operations
• 
Manage creator partnerships: Source, pitch, and recruit relevant tech creators, developer voices, and industry influencers.
• 
Execute campaign logistics: Draft campaign briefs, align timelines, and track deliverables from initial outreach to final publish.

What We're Looking For
• 
Editorial precision: Exceptional written English skills with an instinct for tone, structure, and clarity across social, email, and long-form formats.
• 
Technical translation capability: Comfortable diving into technical platforms, developer dashboards, or AI research to write simple, accurate marketing copy.
• 
AI-first workflow: Habitual use of AI tools for rapid research, content structuring, and drafting.
• 
Platform fluency: Deep, native understanding of content formats, algorithms, and tone across X, LinkedIn, Instagram, and YouTube.
• 
Execution & ownership: Uncompromising attention to detail, strong organizational discipline, and the ability to drive multiple deadlines without hand-holding.

Bonus Points
• 
Hands-on experience with video editing tools or basic script-to-edit workflows.
• 
Familiarity with design tools (Canva, Figma) to quickly mock up assets or social creatives.
• 
Prior experience managing creator outreach, influencer pipelines, or talent operations.
• 
Vernacular fluency in Hindi or a regional Indian language.
• 
Foundational understanding of SEO best practices for written content.

Why Sarvam?
Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems at the frontier of AI with population-scale impact. You'll work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar. High ownership and high impact from day one, AI-first in everything we do, on problems that could change how an entire country works and communicates.

Razorpay is one of India’s leading full-stack financial technology companies, powering the way businesses move, manage, and grow money. Founded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar with a simple vision - to simplify payments for Indian businesses - we’ve since grown into a fintech powerhouse driving India’s digital payment revolution.

Razorpay powers millions of businesses with a smarter, scalable stack that goes beyond transactions to help them truly build and grow.

From building AI-native agentic payments, to AI-assisted fraud detection and real-time risk intelligence to automated reconciliation, smart payouts, and predictive financial insights, we are embedding intelligence across our stack to make money movement faster, safer, and more efficient. In close collaboration with ecosystem partners - including banks, networks, regulators - we are pioneering industry-first solutions that are shaping the next era of fintech

Across India, Singapore and Malaysia, our products span everything from seamless checkouts to payroll automation - powering a fintech ecosystem that’s redefining how money moves across Asia.

Today, that ecosystem supports everyone from early-stage startups to some of India’s largest enterprises, enabling them to accept, process, and disburse payments at scale while expanding into new ways of managing money more efficiently.

Our scale speaks volumes: Razorpay processes $180+ billion in annualized transactions, powering leading businesses like Airbnb, Facebook, WhatsApp, Airtel, CRED, BookmyShow, Zomato, Swiggy, Lenskart, Mirae Asset Capital markets, Indian Oil, National Pension Scheme - and over 100 of India’s unicorns. With strong roots in India and growing operations in Southeast Asia, we are shaping the next chapter of financial technology across the region.

We are backed by global investors including GIC, Peak XV Partners (formerly Sequoia Capital India & SEA), Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Matrix Partners, MasterCard, and Salesforce Ventures, having raised over $740 million to date. Strategic acquisitions - including Ezetap (POS and offline payments), Curlec (Malaysia expansion), BillMe (digital invoicing), and POP (rewards-first UPI) - along with earlier moves in fraud prevention, payroll, and lending, have further strengthened our platform and widened our footprint across Asia.

But what truly sets Razorpay apart is our culture. At Razorpay, ownership is our oxygen - you own what you build, with no micromanagement or red tape, just the runway to make your ideas fly. Learning is a lifestyle - if you’re curious, you’ll feel at home here. People > Pedigree - we hire for attitude, hustle, and hunger more than degrees. Transparency thrives over titles - this is where interns question CXOs and CXOs say “thank you.” Guided by our values of Customer First, Autonomy & Ownership, Agility with Integrity, Transparency, Challenging the status quo and a strong belief that Razorpay grows with Razors,  you’ll be part of a 3000+ strong team building not just products, but the financial infrastructure of the future.

da46c5ad469676b8.description: You will work closely with senior product managers, engineering, design, data, operations, and external partners to deliver a seamless, secure, and high-converting payment experience. You will primarily contribute to execution, analysis, and incremental improvements of payment and UPI flows, while gradually taking more ownership as you grow. Key Responsibilities Assist in maintaining the product roadmap and backlog for payments and UPI in line with the direction set by senior product leaders. Support the definition and optimisation of UPI and payment flows across onboarding, authorization, success/failure, refunds, settlements, and disputes under guidance. Draft clear PRDs, user stories, and acceptance criteria with reviews from senior PMs, and coordinate with Engineering and Design to ensure timely, high-quality delivery. Use dashboards and tools such as Excel or BI tools to monitor funnel performance, success rates, and drop-offs, and support simple A/B tests or experiments to improve conversion. Help manage integrations and daily interactions with external partners like PSPs, banks, gateways, and aggregators, especially around SLAs and production issues. Participate in monitoring system health and reliability, helping coordinate with engineering and operations to quickly diagnose and resolve incidents. Prepare concise product reports, dashboards, and updates for leadership and cross-functional stakeholders. Stay updated on key trends in the payments and UPI ecosystem and share relevant insights with the team as input into product thinking. Required Qualifications 14 years of experience in product management, business analysis, or operations role in a fintech environment. Some exposure to payments or fintech (for example UPI, cards, net banking, wallets, etc. ). Comfort working with data using Excel ; familiarity with SQL or BI tools is an advantage but not mandatory. Experience contributing to the launch or improvement of any user-facing product or internal tool. Ability to write clear documents, break down problems into smaller parts, and prioritize tasks with support from senior PMs. Good to Have Experience collaborating with payment gateways, aggregators, banks, or PSPs in any capacity. Basic understanding of concepts like refunds, settlements, disputes, and fraud or risk controls. Exposure to other payment methods such as cards, net banking, wallets, BNPL, or recurring payments. .
